content.rendered:
On January 18, 1989, Bruce joined an all-star jam band at the fourth annual Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony. Included in the set: Larry Williams’ 1957 hit, “Bony Moronie.”

Bruce can only be seen and heard on guitar in the newly uploaded video below, but since it’s the only known recorded instance of him playing it, I’m sharing and including it here.

It’s a more frenetic performance than the Larry Williams performance; see below for comparison.

Bony Maronie
First performed: January 18, 1989 (New York City, NY)
Last performed: July 2, 1989 (Long Branch, NJ)

© April 27, 2018

excerpt.rendered: New video: Bruce joins an all-start jam at the fourth annual Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and covers Larry Williams’ “Bony Maronie.”

jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce joins Mick Jagger, Stevie Wonder, Tina Turner, and more on Aretha Franklin's 1967 anthem.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Crying
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 1989, Bruce paid tribute to the late, great Roy Orbison by performing Roy's signature ballad at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

jetpack-related-posts.title: I Can’t Turn You Loose
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce Springsteen backs Little Richard and Mick Jagger as they storm their way through Otis Redding's 1965 classic.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Come Together
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Axl Rose's last public appearance for six years was an almost literal last-minute duet with Bruce Springsteen in 1994 at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Hound Dog
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Twice only: Bruce plays one of the all-time great rock and roll songs during surprise appearances at The Stone Pony in the summer of '89.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Born on the Bayou

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce Springsteen and John Fogerty trade lead vocals on a smoking performance of "Born on the Bayou" at the 1993 Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction.
